name: Banila Co Clean It Zero

card.summary: A Korean cleansing balm that melts into oil to dissolve makeup, sunscreen and sebum, helping skin look clean and clear after the first step of double cleansing.
card.aka: Clean It Zero Cleansing Balm Original
card.note: Fragranced product; patch-test if you have sensitive skin.

quick.overview:
Clean It Zero is a cleansing balm from the Korean brand Banila Co. The solid balm melts into an oil on contact with the skin and dissolves makeup, sunscreen and sebum.

Cleaner skin is the appearance payoff: removing residue before a second cleanser leaves skin ready for the rest of a routine. Support for it is mostly product reviews and brand claims; no clinical trials were found.
quick.how: Reviewers describe applying a small scoop to dry skin, massaging it in, adding a little water to emulsify to a milky texture, then rinsing or wiping off with a warm cloth. It is used as a first cleanse, typically followed by a regular cleanser.
quick.risks: Reviewers note it is a fragranced product. A review lists ingredients such as ethylhexyl palmitate, plant extracts and phenoxyethanol, and no parabens, sulfates or mineral oil.

lead: Banila Co Clean It Zero is a cleansing balm sold in several variants, with the Original being best known. It is a solid balm that turns to oil when massaged onto dry skin and removes makeup, sunscreen and sebum.[1]

It helps looks by clearing makeup and SPF thoroughly, which is the first step in the double-cleansing routine popular in Korean skincare. A reviewer states it removes waterproof eye makeup, is a first cleanse only, and did not irritate sensitised skin.[1]
No clinical studies on the product were found. Claims such as brightening come from retailers and the brand rather than independent testing.[2]

chain: Balm melts into oil on skin
Clean skin ready for second cleanse
angle.text: The balm lifts makeup and sunscreen that water-based cleansers can leave behind, so skin looks cleaner after the full routine.

infobox: Ethylhexyl palmitate, acerola extract, tocopheryl acetate

paras: The Original variant is described as a balm with an acerola scent. A review lists ethylhexyl palmitate, cetyl ethylhexanoate, PEG-20 glyceryl triisostearate, phenoxyethanol, tocopheryl acetate and plant extracts, and reports it as paraben-, sulfate- and mineral-oil-free.[1]
Reviewers describe massaging it on dry skin, adding a little water to emulsify, then rinsing or removing with a warm flannel.[1][2]
